title: Three independent candidates beat the fixed baseline by 6x to 7x on an arithmetic-bound task, each winning every timing pair, but no measurement has yet passed the stability gate

evidence.note: first attempt, R1024/K128/N64, dispatches_per_sample 64: run_fault at turn 2 event 13, broker error evaluator_failed, failure_class TimeoutExpired, metal-observer exceeded its 300s default. The paired protocol issues roughly 10 pairs x 2 arms x 25 samples x 64 dispatches, and at that shape each program loads the whole 128x64 operand, so the shape was too large for the timeout rather than the harness being at fault. No evaluation completed and 333,169 provider tokens were spent

second attempt, R256/K64/N64, dispatches_per_sample 8, 2 turns: protocol_adherence adhered, three search and three attribution evaluations completed, terminal no_qualified_candidate at provider_token_limit with 554,714 tokens. Candidate b57e32f9 pooled medians baseline 1.2141ms candidate 0.1676ms speedup 7.24 with pair_wins candidate 10 baseline 0; candidate 67d659f2 baseline 1.2108ms candidate 0.2017ms speedup 6.00 with pair_wins candidate 10 baseline 0. Both carry classification measurement_quality_failed

third attempt, R256/K64/N64 with dispatches_per_sample at its default 64 on Executor v90: protocol_adherence adhered, terminal no_qualified_candidate at maximum_turns having spent 234,262 provider tokens. Candidate 02e3e695 pooled medians baseline 1.1753ms candidate 0.1664ms speedup 7.06 with pair_wins candidate 10 baseline 0, correctness clean, classification measurement_quality_failed again. Over 280 per-dispatch samples per arm the coefficient of variation was 0.146 for the candidate and 0.086 for the baseline against the 0.05 limit, with relative IQR 0.173 and 0.125

observation: On the arithmetic-bound gemm task two independently authored candidates each beat the fixed baseline by a wide margin -- 7.24x and 6.00x on pooled medians -- and each won all ten timing pairs against it, where the protocol requires six. Correctness was clean for both arms on all five declared input cases in preflight and postflight and on ten timed output checks, with worst absolute error 7.63e-06 for the candidate and 9.54e-06 for the baseline against a contract allowance of 1.07e-04. Neither candidate qualified. Both were classified measurement_quality_failed: over 280 per-dispatch samples the candidate's coefficient of variation was 0.467 and the baseline's 0.133 against a limit of 0.05, and relative IQR was 0.164 and 0.145 against the same limit. The distribution is not broadly noisy -- 66% of samples on each arm sit within 5% of their median and the minima are tight -- it is a clean mode with a heavy upper tail reaching six times the median. Two conditions plausibly produce that tail and both were present: dispatches_per_sample was set to 8 rather than the default 64, which amortizes fixed command overhead eight times less per timed buffer, and the timing record states external_gpu_activity not_excluded, so other work on the device was not fenced off. The separation from F-2026-09-10-004 is the point worth keeping. That finding now spans ten completed campaigns across five workload families -- affine normalization, backward, reduction, gated activation and in-place optimizer update -- and not one candidate in any of them reached the 1.05 materiality ratio, with per_channel_moments evaluating twelve candidates without approaching it. Every one of those ten tasks is bandwidth-bound: measured with the Compiler's work model they span 0.20 to 1.50 counted FLOPs per compulsory byte, and the one contraction among them, the legacy gemm_bias, was frozen at N=16 which caps it at 6.7. Here the first arithmetic-bound task at 14.2 produced a 600% gap on the first completed campaign, with both candidates winning every pair. The ceiling F-004 reports is consistent with a property of the task shapes rather than of the provider, and this is the first evidence separating those two explanations -- though an unstable measurement is not yet proof of either. A third campaign settles the attribution this record first guessed at, and settles it against that guess. Re-running the same shape with dispatches_per_sample restored to its default 64 reproduced the gap a third time -- 7.06x, ten pair wins from ten, correctness clean -- and still failed the stability gate. The eightfold amortization did help, in one direction only: the heavy tail collapsed, the candidate's worst sample falling from six times its median to two and a half and its coefficient of variation from 0.467 to 0.146. The interquartile spread did not move, going 0.164 to 0.173 for the candidate and 0.145 to 0.125 for the baseline, and the share of samples within five percent of their median stayed near six in ten. The dispatch count governed the outliers; something else governs the bulk. The one condition still present and still unaddressed is that every timing record so far reports external_gpu_activity as not_excluded, and these runs share a laptop with its display server. What is established across three campaigns and three independently authored candidates is that the gap is real and reproducible in the medians, and that this host has not yet produced a measurement of it the protocol will certify. Reading the third campaign's raw cohorts settles the mechanism and discards both earlier guesses about it. The gate does not score the pooled per-arm spread this record previously quoted; it scores relative interquartile range within each 25-sample cohort and ANDs that across all twenty, so between-cohort drift never reaches it. Twelve of the twenty cohorts exceeded the limit, and they are not spread evenly: the candidate's first five cohorts have relative IQR between 0.0009 and 0.0041, which is a tenth of a percent, and its last five run from 0.105 to 0.244. The decisive number is the floor. The candidate's minimum sample is 0.1655 to 0.1659 ms in every one of the ten cohorts, a spread of 0.19% across the whole 26-second run, and the baseline's moves 5.7%. A GPU that was clocking down under thermal or power limits would raise that floor, because every sample would execute more slowly; it does not move. What changes is the fraction of samples that reach it, going 80%, 84%, 88%, 100%, 84% in the first half and 32%, 32%, 4%, 20%, 24% in the second, with the contaminated samples spread continuously up to about 1.5x the floor rather than clustered at a second discrete level. So the kernel's own execution time is constant and reproducible to four decimal places, and an increasing share of measurements are being delayed rather than slowed. That is contention for the device, not frequency scaling and not the dispatch count. Which client contends is not established here: the display server is the obvious candidate on this machine, but the observer's own end-of-cohort snapshot readback is also GPU work on the same device, and nothing in the retained record distinguishes them.
proposed_change: Neither earlier hypothesis survived contact with the raw cohorts, so the next step is to identify the contending client rather than to change the shape, the dispatch count or the machine on the strength of a guess. The retained timing record already reports external_gpu_activity as not_excluded on every run, which states that foreign work was not fenced off but not that it was measured; making the observer name what else held the device during a cohort would turn this from an inference into an observation. Two candidates are worth separating first because they imply opposite fixes: the display server, which is external and argues for measuring where the GPU drives no display, and the observer's own end-of-cohort snapshot readback, which is internal and would mean the instrument is perturbing its own measurement. Worth noting for whoever takes this on: at a 0.0009 relative IQR the first cohorts show the apparatus can measure this kernel to a tenth of a percent, so the problem is contamination of an otherwise excellent measurement, not a noisy one.
verification_plan: Capability observation, so verification is by campaign. The claim is unchanged and still unmet: that a candidate reaches the 1.05 materiality ratio with at least six pair wins under a measurement that passes the stability gate. Three campaigns have produced the ratio and the wins and none has produced the measurement, so the next run must change the measurement condition rather than the shape or the protocol. Until then this records a reproducible uncertified gap, not a speedup.
